newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amic, Japanese firms in 90 mln rand venture.
newsitem.headline: Amic, Japanese firms in 90 mln rand venture.

text.p: Anglo American Industrial Corp on Friday announced the signing of a joint venture with Komatsu Ltd and Itochu Corp, which represents 90 million rand direct investment by the two Japanese firms.
The joint venture is between Komatsu and Itochu and Amic's wholly-owned subsidiary Amquip to establish a new company Komatsu Southern Africa (Pty) Ltd (Komatsu SA).

"The formation of Komatsu SA represents a substantial direct investment of approximately 90 million rand by two major Japanese enterprises while retaining a strong local interest through Amquip," Amic chairman Leslie Boyd said.
The shareholding in Komatsu SA will be 50 percent Komatsu Ltd, 30 percent Amquip and 20 percent Itochu.
The deal is effective from January 31.
The turnover for Komatsu SA for 1997 is expected to exceed 550 million rand.

"The joint venture is a significant expression of confidence in the mining and construction equipment industry in South Africa and a major financial and moral commitment to its future," said Maurice Allen, chairman of the new Komatsu SA.

Komatsu SA has acquired the ongoing business of Komdresco, a general partnership owned by Amquip (50 percent) and Intool International BV (formerly Indresco Netherlands BV), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Global Industrial Technologies of Dallas, Texas (50 percent).
The primary business of Komdresco is the supply of equipment and services to the mining and construction industry.
Komatsu SA will also acquire the shares of Tswana Equipment (Pty) Ltd, presently owned by Amquip (50 percent) and Indresco Netherlands (50 percent).
